name: Castell de Miravet – Ebro crossing viewpoint
story: The Templar castle of Miravet stands above one of the stretches where the Army of the Ebro crossed the river by boat and footbridge in the early hours of 25 July 1938. It took the Nationalists by surprise. The Republican aim was to relieve pressure on Valencia and restore the link with the central zone, and the attack advanced up to 20–40 km in the first days. The castle now holds one of the network's interpretation exhibitions on the objectives and course of the battle, and it gives a good view of how the river shaped the fighting.
see: A 12th–13th century Templar castle with a permanent exhibition on the Battle of the Ebro, and views over the river, the ferry and the village.
plan: Tue–Sat 10:00–17:30 (to 19:00 May–Sep), Sun 10:00–15:00, closed Mondays; €7 (reduced €5). The traditional river ferry (pas de barca) below the village is worth combining with a visit.
